ve.beiEinbringen: If you introduce the proposal today
ve.naechsterSchritt: You open parliamentary debate. You can then negotiate compromises and win votes. The programme has not yet been approved.
ve.zeitplan: If approved: ready from {ab}, ends on {bis}. Duration: {tage} days. The next monthly accounts show the effects actually achieved.
ve.partnerUnzufrieden: The base proposal leaves these coalition partners’ demands unmet: {parteien}.
ve.stimmenDetails: Review faction demands and possible reactions
ve.verhandeln: After introducing the proposal, you will find concrete paths to a majority through clause changes and faction talks. Compromises can change the budget, duration and political consequences.
ve.beiAnnahme: If the base proposal is approved
ve.beiAblehnung: If the base proposal is rejected
ve.ablehnung: Rejection books no programme budget. Political capital already spent remains spent; government trust falls by 0.5 and approval by 0.4 points.
ve.vorbehalt: Calculated for the planned vote using today’s situation and known support-agreement deadlines. Later decisions, crises and coalition changes can alter the result. None of these reactions has been applied yet.
ve.kursAbrechnung: The new allocation priority applies immediately
ve.kursFolgen: Priorities change how scarce goods are distributed. They create no additional stocks. The monthly report shows whether civilians or the front actually receive better supplies. Party reactions apply immediately when priorities change.
ve.kursRisiko: {name}: loyalty {vorher} → {nachher}. Below 20, withdrawal threatens at the next coalition review on {datum}: {sitze} seats would be lost, leaving {rest}. Further decisions and monthly effects can still change support.
